data.headline: S&P futures shorts narrow as the Treasury curve flattens
data.summary: Between October 27 and November 3, leveraged funds reduced their E-mini S&P 500 net short while asset managers increased their net long. The ten-year minus two-year Treasury spread subsequently narrowed to 35 basis points on November 6.

bull.text: The E-mini S&P 500 asset-manager net long rose from 923,449 to 928,584 contracts. The leveraged-fund net short fell from 400,604 to 372,318 contracts.

bear.text: The two-year yield rose 5 basis points to 4.51% from November 5 to 6. Higher benchmarks can raise short-term refinancing costs for index constituents whose borrowing resets with market rates.

watch.text: The ten-year minus two-year spread narrowed from 38 to 35 basis points. The impact on lenders depends on funding costs, how quickly assets reprice and credit losses.

limitations: The Treasury yields are dated November 6. This report has no verified ETF closing-price or return observation.
The CFTC observations are weekly futures positions as of November 3. ETF flows and investor intent require separate evidence.
